abstract: This study focuses on the food and housing expenditures of households relative to their disposable incomes, utilizing a unique opportunity of merged national-level data from the Household Budget Survey and EU-Statistics on Income and Living Conditions in Czechia (2020–2023). The study considers both Engel’s law on food expenditures and Schwabe’s law on housing expenditures by verifying their implications for poverty measures. Interpretation of the two laws assumes that households spending the same shares of their income on food/housing are equally well-off, and a specific level of food-/housing-income ratio is then used as a poverty threshold, which implies that absolute household income is irrelevant to their economic well-being. Both laws are valid in Czechia: relative food and housing expenditures are decreasing with income. We proxy households’ economic well-being using both subjective and objective indicators of household economic well-being: within sub-groups with similar relative food/housing expenditures, absolute income still significantly affects the economic well-being of households. This effect is stronger for those designated as the poorest than it is for those deemed richest. We claim that the validity of Engel’s and Schwabe’s laws does not straightforwardly imply that having the same relative food/housing expenditures means that households are equally well-off. KEYWORDS: Czechia EU food expenditures household expenses housing expenditures JEL CLASSIFICATION: I32 I30 Acknowledgements The national EU-SILC (ŽP) and CZ-HBS (SRÚ) datafiles were made available on the basis of a contract between the Czech Statistical Office and the Institute of Sociology of the Czech Academy of Sciences. We are grateful for additional advice provided by the corresponding department of the Czech Statistical Office. Responsibility for conclusions drawn from the data and any errors lies entirely with the authors.
abstract_zh: 本研究聚焦于家庭食品与住房支出相对于其可支配收入的变动规律，利用捷克共和国2020-2023年家庭预算调查与欧盟收入与生活条件统计数据的全国层面合并数据这一独特契机。研究同时验证了恩格尔定律（食品支出）与施瓦贝定律（住房支出）对贫困测度的含义。对这两条定律的解读假定：食品/住房支出占收入比例相同的家庭具有同等经济福利水平，并以此类食品/住房收入比的特定水平作为贫困线阈值，这意味着家庭绝对收入与其经济福利无关。两条定律在捷克均成立：食品与住房的相对支出随收入增加而递减。我们采用主观与客观两类经济福利指标衡量家庭经济状况：在具有相似相对食品/住房支出的子群体中，绝对收入仍显著影响家庭经济福利，且该效应在贫困群体中强于富裕群体。我们认为，恩格尔定律与施瓦贝定律的有效性并不能直接推导出"相同相对食品/住房支出意味着家庭同等富裕"的结论。
authors: Martina Mysíková Michaela Jirková Jiří Večerník Institute of Sociology of the Czech Academy of Sciences, Prague
title: The role of food and housing expenditures in household economic well-being: evidence from Czechia
title_zh: 食品与住房支出在家庭经济福祉中的作用：来自捷克共和国的证据

abstract: The civil service examination system of ancient China, Keju system, is praised as an institution prompting social mobility and stability. This study investigates how the operation of this system, the performance of candidates affected social stability of China in the 18th century. By a model of ‘Rob-Fight’ Game, we prove how divergence between de jure and de facto power causes social instability. Using panel data of 260 prefectures during 1736–1795, we find more newly presented scholars (Jinshi) were associated with a higher frequency of homicides for sexual and marital affairs. Though we consider the concern about ranks of new scholars and law enforcement by law officers, our finding remains. Using the interaction of long-term fixed quota for successful candidates and total number of new scholars as the instrument, we show that our finding remains. The development of non-agricultural economy could impede such effects of Keju performance while the civil education played a trivial role.
